paper_title: ChARM Character-based Act-adaptive Reward Modeling for Advanced   Role-Playing Language Agents
caption: The character distribution in RoleplayPref consists of 3 primary categories and 13 subcategories.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The diagram illustrates the distribution of character types within the RoleplayPref framework, categorizing characters into three primary sectors: Virtual Characters, Custom Characters, and Real Characters. There are a total of 13 subcategories represented, with the sectors color-coded for differentiation. The Virtual Characters section is shown in light blue, including Movie Characters, Teleplay Characters, Novel Characters, and Game Characters. The Custom Characters sector is depicted in pink, while the Real Characters sector is highlighted in green, further divided into subcategories such as Scientists, Artists, Athletes, Writers, Musicians, Actors, and Influencers. The diagram includes labels on the slices, and the Real Characters sector visually stands out due to its green coloration.
model_annotations.English: The chart illustrates the character distribution in RoleplayPref, categorizing characters into three primary groups: Virtual Characters, Custom Characters, and Real Characters. The categories include Virtual Characters (blue, approximately 40%), Custom Characters (pink, approximately 10%), Real Characters (green, approximately 30%), as well as six subcategories under Real Characters: Scientists (light green, approximately 5%), Artists (light green, approximately 5%), Athletes (light green, approximately 5%), Writers (light green, approximately 5%), Musicians (light green, approximately 5%), Actors (light green, approximately 5%), and Influencers (light green, approximately 5%). The slices do not include percentage labels inside them, and there is no visible legend.
